Daily learnings — what the machine learned, every day

This section re-reads the latest night studies and the latest prediction-space tracker report on every render, so it refreshes on the nightly regen with no manual step. Each night's study is the machine's lesson log: what it got right, what it got wrong, and what it will build next. Candidate rules stay candidates here — nothing in this section adopts a rule by itself.

2026-10-24 night study — 9 owner-placed slips (s1–s9), 47 system legs + 2 tracked owner legs, $10.50 staked ($9.50 cash + $1.00 bonus bet), all 9 tickets lost, $0 returned. All 47 system legs settled on live-watch evidence (see corrections below): 26 hit / 21 missed (55.3%). The 0-for-9 headline stands on either the re-evaluation record or the corrected record. No single injury killed the night. The night died the ordinary way: 19 unique system deaths spread across all 9 slips, 9 of them tail-zone landings, and winners stranded across slips that each carried at least one killer.
  • 1. OBSERVATION — Below-floor lines: any under whose line sits below the printed floor (Aaron Wiggins, Herro, Ellis) must carry a "BELOWFLOOR" marker on the card; the cushion verdict cannot print CUSHION on a below-floor line without that marker.
  • 2. CANDIDATE LAW — Flag veto: a leg carrying STINTWARNING + MINFRAGILE together (Schroder's exact pair) requires a second corroborating input or it does not ship on a multi-leg slip.
  • 3. CANDIDATE LAW — TIGHT exclusion enforced: P.J.-type TIGHT legs are excluded from placed builds (bettor seat's CUSHION-only rule, already law for the seat, proposed for the forge).
  • 4. OBSERVATION — BLOWOUTBENCHRISK fired 9 times, explained 0 deaths: demote it from a leg-level flag to a game-level note until it shows a death.
  • 5. CANDIDATE LAW — Matchup-layer stat-match gate: a matchup record whose scale does not match the leg's stat (Mobley AST vs a PTS-scale record) is SILENT, never AGREED/WARNED.
  • 6. OBSERVATION — Record the placed price for every leg at placement time (screenshots show only some); without it, closing-line-value audit is impossible for SGPMAX slips.

Web Knots — every entry tied to its ledger block

A web knot is the entry's tie to the ledger web. Category is the entry class (placed ticket, proposed build, settlement record, correction record, ledger record). Case is the night plus the entry title. Relevance is the tie strength from the chain itself: settled tie when a SETTLEMENT block carries the entry index, direct tie when a PLACEMENT block does, recorded tie when a BUILD block does, untied when no block carries it. Tapping a WEB KNOT chip on any entry, or any knot row below, lands on that knot's tied-block card here and offers a jump to the chain section; the raw chain file is linked at the bottom of this page. The Widow patrols this web-knots section anchor only — never individual entry rows and never knot chips. Spine tie (W1-L7 event log, read at render time): gameshark surface, event append, height 593, hash e9cd34fe1b0c…, at 2026-10-26T18:14:43+00:00. A knot tap resolves through this envelope shape: event, height, hash, surface, at. Bridge citation: GameShark BRIDGE block h=1622 names FUSION-7 tip h=506 (audit block h=506).

Player lookup — 2025-26 bands + 2026-27 to date

Season band = full 2025-26 regular season (floor p10 / natural median / ceiling p90, minutes-adjusted). 2026-27 averages cover 28 games (2026-10-20 → 2026-10-23) — a tiny sample, labeled as such on every card. Players with no 2025-26 profile show their team and current-season averages, with the missing season stated in words. Search a name above; players appear here. Each card carries the player picture (initials where no photo is on file), tendency rates, and one separate game-by-game graph for every stat line in the logs, covering every game on file. Every graph carries MJ's projected next-game value as a gold diamond with a dashed line past the last game. The full profile shows all twelve graphs at once; list cards build them on one tap to keep search fast on phones. MJ's heating, falling, and bounce-back lists live in MJ's Study Board just below. A player with no game log on file gets that stated in words, never a blank.

MJ's Study Board — heating up, falling below norm, due for a bounce back

MJ patrols this page while it is open, studying every graph and every number on it. His projections refresh with the nightly data, so the studying never stops. A projection is the recency-weighted median of the player's own games — the same engine the grader trusts for its natural line. It is an estimate, never a promise. Bands here cover ALL games on file (the same games the charts plot). A player whose role changed recently (new team, new minutes) can look hot or cold because the band covers his old role too — the chart itself shows whether it is form or a role change.

Per-minute / per-possession rates — the opportunity layer

The equation, in plain words: projected final = current value + rate x remaining opportunity. Minutes version: remaining minutes = the player's mean minutes minus the minutes he has already played. Possessions version: remaining team possessions = team pace x clock left, times the player's share of his team's possessions. Every projection from these rates is an ESTIMATE — never banked, never a settlement, only the final boxscore counts.
How the rates are built. Per-minute rates are exact, from box minutes. Per-possession rates use TRUE on-court possessions: the archive's 255,430 possessions all carry both teams' lineups (255,430 with lineups, 100.00%), so a player's offensive possessions are the possessions where his name is in his team's attacking lineup — no minutes-proration anywhere. 26,587 of 26,587 log games matched an archive game; 582 players carry rates. One coverage gap, named: Patrick Baldwin Jr. on 2026-01-21 logged 5 minutes with zero possessions on court (a lineup-tracking gap in that one game). Offensive stats (points, assists, shots, turnovers) are rated per offensive possession on court; rebounds, steals and blocks per possession on court, either end.
Shot attempts are the opportunity measure. FGA per offensive possession says how often a player shoots when his team has the ball — a high number means he always has the chance to reach a scoring line. Leaders below, season window, players with 20 or more games.

Backtest verdict (2026-10-26, honest). As a PRE-GAME predictor, rates do not beat the raw log distributions: leave-one-out over 26,583 player-games — NEUTRAL on points, rebounds, field-goal attempts, makes and three-point attempts (within 2%), WORSE on assists, three-point makes, turnovers, steals and blocks (low-count stats, where the median beats a smooth projection). On 54 settled 2026-10-25 legs, rate-implied probabilities scored Brier 0.321 against the grader's 0.239 — overconfident, because rate x minutes ignores per-game scoring variance beyond minutes. So rates stay DATA: their job is the live scaling the static distribution cannot do mid-game, plus the opportunity measure. No weight, gate or threshold changed on their account. Full per-player rates live in ledger.db tables player_rates, player_game_possessions and team_pace.

Player DNA Radar — one axis per tendency

The same radar that appears on every player lookup card, on demand here. Type a name and show it. Axes are in-cushion, ceiling-break, floor-hit, and neutral-landing percent, drawn as SVG from the season band and the game log loaded alongside this page. One shape per stat, with the exact percentages in the table under the radar.

Game index — 1307 games

Every archived game: date, matchup, final score, event id, play count. Search a date (2026-10-23) or a team (MIA, NY, BOS…) above. Latest night shown by default:

Play-by-play — indexed here, not embedded

The full play-by-play — every substitution, every possession, every score, every stat — lives in archive/games/<date>/<event_id>.json: 1307 games, 633,111 plays, 883MB (1239 games before 2026-10-01 including the audited 1,231-game 2025-26 regular season, plus 68 games from 2026-10-20 → 2026-10-23). A phone page cannot hold 883MB, so the bytes are not in this page — but every game is indexed above by date, teams and event id, and any single game (boxscore, plays, possessions) can be pulled on request. Averages from the start of this season are in the player cards above, computed from those same archive files.

Leg Connection Map — a night as a graph

Tickets on top, shared-core players in gold in the middle, shared games at the bottom. A gold line means that ticket shares a core player with another ticket that night. A blue line means it shares a core game. Core means appearing on two or more tickets that night. The 2026-10-25 night is hypothetical, watched not placed, and is the default because it is the only full night set on file outside the ledger entries. Ledger nights come from the entries already on this page.

Deep-Sea Explorer — full history dive

Every leg row recorded for players on this page, with its band landing, filterable by player, game or ticket text, stat market, and result, paged at 50 per page with no cap. This is not the stranded-winners view in Diagnosis: that view keeps its own 60-item display slice, untouched by this section.

Live Ocean — live-watch view shell

Never banked off a live feed, only the final boxscore counts. A live number is a watch number, not a settlement number. Live data fetching is a separate concern and is not wired in this patch: the slots below fill only when a live feed calls window.gsOcean.setLive with a live-game object, and nothing in this section writes a score, a grade, or a ledger row.
Never banked off a live feed, only the final boxscore counts.
Clock: awaiting live update · Quarter: awaiting live update · Score: awaiting live update
Data hook: window.gsOcean.setLive(game) where game carries game, clock, quarter, away, away_score, home, home_score, box rows, and is_final. When is_final is false the banner stays on watch-only. When is_final is true the banner says the final boxscore is the only version that counts.

Matchup Mirror — a player against his position's defense

Pick a player and the defense he faces. The page shows his modal position from archive box lines, his season band, what that defense allows per game to his position group over the full 2025-26 season, the same cell for 2026-27 to date, and his own logged games against that team. Every sample size is printed. This is team-vs-position, never man-to-man: the archive does not attribute opponent rebounds or assists to individual defenders. The old 4-day window is not used here: the matchup sample is the full-season pipeline, and the 4-day current-season averages on the lookup cards stay labeled as a tiny sample where they are.

Player Card Generator — lookup card as an exportable image

Type a name, see the card, export it as a PNG image at 1080 by 1350 with large legible type. The photo comes from the verified headshot file only: a player with no verified photo gets initials on the card and on the image, never a guessed photo. The same export button sits on every full lookup card.

Band Depth Plot — the last 20 games against the band

One dot per game from the new 20-game actuals store, with the season band lines drawn across it. A player with fewer than 20 logged games shows exactly the games on file, and the count says so. This store is separate from the per-leg bands: it is actual game scores, last 20 first, not tracker history.

Ledger Time Machine — replay a past render

Every render saves a snapshot with its totals, its weights, and its bars. Pick a snapshot to replay it exactly as that render recorded it. This replays render state; it does not re-simulate any game, and it never rewrites a score. The page embeds the most recent snapshots; older ones stay as snapshot files.

Change Radar + Shark Sonar — what changed between two renders

Pick two snapshots. Every changed total, every changed weight, and every changed bar is listed by name: player, stat, and field, with the before and after values. Sonar pings the loudest bar changes first. A weight change between two renders shows here as a named diff, not as a silent drift.
